name: Northside
label: Factory Records
lede: Four lads from Blackley and Moston sold out their first gig by word of mouth, got signed by Tony Wilson from the back of the room, and saw their first single banned by the BBC.

eras.title: Word of mouth at the Boardwalk
eras.text: Northside came out of Blackley and Moston in north Manchester just as the city's guitar-and-dance bands were filling the papers. Within a few months of forming they had a sold-out debut, a Happy Mondays support and Tony Wilson watching.

years.src: Louder Than War · Live4ever · Wikipedia: Northside
years.h: Dermo and Cliff Ogier start a band in north Manchester
years.p: Warren "Dermo" Dermody sings and writes the words, Cliff Ogier plays bass, Paul Walsh drums and Michael Upton plays guitar. They rehearse at the Holland Street Sports Centre in Miles Platting.

years.h: The Boardwalk sells out for Northside's first gig
years.p: With no record out yet, the Manchester club fills on word of mouth. Tony Wilson is standing at the back.
years.xp: "He was at the back of the room and loved it," Dermo told Live4ever. Wilson signed them to Factory Records early the next year.

years.h: The power fails at the Free Trade Hall, and Dermo keeps talking
years.p: On their third gig, supporting [[Happy Mondays|01f4fb92-6bf0-4de5-83dc-3fe194e763bf]], the Free Trade Hall loses its power. Dermo keeps the crowd entertained until it comes back.

eras.title: Factory, and a BBC ban
eras.text: Wilson signed Northside early in 1990, and Factory put out two singles in five months. The first was kept off daytime Radio 1 and charted anyway; the second went Top 40.

years.cap: Music-press page on Northside and Tony Wilson, March 3, 1990
years.h: Tony Wilson signs them; Timmy Walsh takes the guitar
years.p: Factory signs Northside, and before the first single Michael Upton is replaced by Timmy Walsh.

years.cap: Dermo, Cliff Ogier, Paul Walsh and Timmy Walsh, c. 1990
years.src: Louder Than War · Live4ever · Wikipedia: Northside
years.h: The BBC bans "Shall We Take a Trip". It charts anyway
years.p: The debut, a double A-side with "Moody Places", opens with the letters L-S-D, and BBC daytime radio wouldn't touch it. It reached No. 50 with no daytime airplay.
years.xp:
[[Ian Broudie|45154afb-9a09-41bf-a39c-654c3f497c08]] produced it. Dermo said the ban held until 2004, when [[Marc Riley|9b872fea-1c8e-42f8-878d-c8356de79bba]] played it on the BBC.

Granada TV picked it up instead: the song was the theme for Soccer Night through the 1990s.

years.cap: "North Proles," a music-press feature on Northside, October 27, 1990
years.p: FAC 298. The video was shot on the roof of Manchester's Arndale Centre.

years.h: Factory's Manchester bands take over the New Music Seminar
years.p: Dermo remembers playing New York's New Music Seminar alongside Happy Mondays, [[A Guy Called Gerald|b343730d-a34e-44d5-9191-a83f00231716]] and [[808 State|36f35db0-bc09-43e7-8650-a123224943c7]], and a night at the Sound Factory.

eras.title: Rockfield, Top of the Pops and American radio
eras.text: Northside made their album with Ian Broudie across three studios, then had their best year: a Top 20 album at home and a single that did better on American alternative radio than it did in Britain.

years.h: Broudie makes the album in Wrexham, Liverpool and Rockfield
years.p: Chicken Rhythms is recorded at Windings in Wrexham, Amazon in Liverpool and Rockfield in Monmouthshire, engineered by Cenzo Townsend.

years.src: Wikipedia: Northside · Louder Than War · Live4ever
years.h: "Take 5" gets them on Top of the Pops from outside the Top 40
years.p: FAC 308 peaked at No. 40 in Britain. In the US it went to No. 5 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart that October.
years.xp:
The band played Top of the Pops on June 6, 1991, with the single at No. 41, which almost never happened. "We had to mime," Dermo said.

He also says "Take 5" was No. 1 in Canada until [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] knocked it off.

years.cap: Northside on a stone stairway, c. 1991
years.src: Louder Than War · Live4ever · Wikipedia: Northside
yt: "Tour de World" live at Manchester Academy, June 1991
years.p: Ten songs on vinyl, eleven on CD with "My Rising Star" added. Tours followed across Europe and in Japan, with festival slots at Roskilde and Dala Rock.

eras.title: The second album stays in the can
eras.text: Northside recorded a follow-up in 1992. Factory went bankrupt in November before it could come out, and the band split.

years.h: A second album is made at Peter Hook's studio in Rochdale
years.p: Northside record it with producer Rex Sargeant at Suite 16, the studio co-owned by [[Peter Hook|73e7c483-9f3e-4a72-a359-582452fbaeac]].

years.h: Factory goes bankrupt, and Northside split up
years.p: The second album stays in the can.

eras.title: Dermo carries the name
eras.text: Wilson was still talking them up in 1995. Dermo brought the name back in 2006, and the original four got back together in 2013.

years.h: Wilson's verdict, three years after the end
years.p: Wilson called Northside "a stunning live band" and said Dermo "was the only person in Manchester not trying to be [[Ian Brown|182d5d8a-94c7-4ef4-8222-a1838353a37b]]".

years.h: Northside play Leeds and Manchester with Dermo the only original
years.p: [[Marc Riley|9b872fea-1c8e-42f8-878d-c8356de79bba]] played "Shall We Take a Trip" on BBC 6 Music the same year.

years.cap: The reunited original four, Timmy Walsh far right, c. 2013
years.h: All four originals are back for an English tour
years.p: Dermo, Ogier and the two Walshes tour England in April and May 2014.

years.h: Cherry Red collects the Factory years on two CDs
years.p: Shall We Take a Trip: The Factory Recordings 1990–1991 gathers the singles and the album.

eras.title: Losing Timmy, signing again
eras.text: Timmy Walsh died in 2019. Six years on, the album got a reissue on London Records and the band signed a new deal.

years.p: Walsh died suddenly. For more than 25 years he had worked as a sound engineer for Mersey TV, on Brookside and then Hollyoaks.

years.cap: Dermo on stage at Gorilla, Manchester, April 2025
years.src: Jace Media · God Is in the TV
years.h: Chicken Rhythms is reissued on London Records
years.p: The 1991 album comes back out, 34 years on.

years.h: Northside sign to Venture Records for a new album
years.p: The band said a new album is planned for 2027. In March, Dermo's heart attack had pulled them off a Happy Mondays support tour.
